## Proposal: Set a January 15 H-1B Registration Intake Deadline

For the coming cap season, I propose that we set January 15 as our internal deadline for H-1B registration intake. This is a process change to give us and our clients more time to prepare carefully—not a response to clients being late. Our current approach is to send the questionnaire whenever an employer asks, without giving them a target date. One HR contact told me she would have been happy to send everything in January if we had asked.

Last season, we filed 14 registrations for six employer clients, and nine arrived in the final week of February. Rosa logged roughly 11 hours of overtime the week the registration window opened. That crunch reflects our process as much as anything else: we had not given employers a date to work toward. A January deadline would spread the work out and leave time to follow up on missing information.

It would also give us more room to catch problems before filing. Brightwater Analytics sent a beneficiary’s passport scan two days before the window opened. The passport had expired in October, and we caught it because Rosa checked the dates. Registration itself is simple, but errors can be costly; the wrong passport information can invalidate a selection. The $215 registration fee per beneficiary is already something employers budget for in Q1, and January 15 is realistic: HR teams are back from the holidays and budgets are set.

**What would change:**
- Send engagement letters and a one-page questionnaire during the week of December 7.
- Set January 15 as the intake deadline, with later submissions handled case by case.
- Have Rosa own the tracker, giving her a clear six weeks to chase gaps before the deadline.

If Marcus agrees when we meet Thursday, we can send the December letters and questionnaires on schedule. The goal is a more predictable, attentive service for employers—and a manageable runway for our team.
